title: GST 114 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER 2 ( MAJOR WORD CLASSES )
subject: GST 114

questions.question: Which term refers to a class of words sharing grammatical traits?
questions.explanation: Word classes group words based on shared grammatical characteristics (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which categories form the major parts of speech?
questions.explanation: The major parts of speech are nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which term defines a word that names a person, place, or thing?
questions.explanation: A noun is defined as a word used to name a person, place, animal, thing, or idea (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type gives a specific name to a particular person or place?
questions.explanation: Proper nouns are specific names given to particular persons, places, or things (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type refers to general items or people and accepts plural markers?
questions.explanation: Common nouns are general names that accept plural markers like s, es, and ies (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type names physical things that can be seen or touched?
questions.explanation: Concrete nouns name physical things that can be seen or touched (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type refers to ideas or qualities existing only in the mind?
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns refer to ideas or qualities that exist only in the mind (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun category represents entities that can be counted and pluralized?
questions.explanation: Count nouns represent entities that can be counted and pluralized (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type refers to a group of people or things as one entity?
questions.explanation: Collective nouns refer to a group of people or things considered as one entity (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which function does a noun perform as the performer of an action?
questions.explanation: The subject of a sentence is the performer of the action (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which function does a noun perform when receiving the action of a verb?
questions.explanation: A direct object receives the action of the verb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which function does a noun perform when completing a linking verb?
questions.explanation: A complement is used to complete the predicate of a sentence (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which function does a noun perform when following a preposition?
questions.explanation: A noun functioning as the object of a preposition comes after a preposition (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which function does a noun perform when renaming another noun beside it?
questions.explanation: In apposition, two nouns are used next to each other to refer to the same thing (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which case is used for a noun acting as the subject of a verb?
questions.explanation: The subjective case is used for a noun acting as the subject of a verb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which case is used for a noun acting as the object of a verb?
questions.explanation: The objective case is used for a noun acting as the object of a verb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which case indicates ownership and often uses an apostrophe?
questions.explanation: The possessive case indicates ownership and often uses an apostrophe (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which case is used when directly addressing a person by name?
questions.explanation: The vocative case is used when directly addressing a person by name (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which plural form is created by adding s or es to a singular noun?
questions.explanation: Regular plural nouns are formed by adding s or es to the singular form (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which plural form changes the word entirely rather than adding s or es?
questions.explanation: Irregular plurals are formed in various ways, such as changing the word entirely (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which noun type lacks a singular form and is always plural?
questions.explanation: Plural invariable nouns have no singular forms and are always plural (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which part of speech states the action performed by the subject?
questions.explanation: Verbs are words that state the action performed by the subject (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type is limited by the subject and shows tense?
questions.explanation: A finite verb is limited by the subject and shows tense (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type takes a direct object to complete its meaning?
questions.explanation: A transitive verb takes a direct object to complete its meaning (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type does not take a direct object?
questions.explanation: Intransitive verbs do not take direct objects (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type describes a state of being rather than an action?
questions.explanation: Stative verbs are primarily used to describe a state of being (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type refers to verbs that perform physical actions?
questions.explanation: Action verbs refer to all verbs which are non-stative and perform actions (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb type indicates that the subject causes an action to happen?
questions.explanation: Causative verbs indicate that the subject causes an action to be performed (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which auxiliary verb is used to form perfect tenses and passive voice?
questions.explanation: Primary auxiliaries like have, be, and do are used to form perfect tenses and passive voice (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which auxiliary verb expresses possibility, ability, or necessity?
questions.explanation: Modal auxiliary verbs express possibility, ability, necessity, and other moods (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which non-finite verb form uses to plus the base verb?
questions.explanation: The to-infinitive is formed by using to plus the base form of the verb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb form ends in ing and functions as a noun?
questions.explanation: A gerund is a verb form ending in ing that performs the functions of a noun (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which verb form functions as an adjective and can end in ing or ed?
questions.explanation: A participle functions as an adjective and can be present or past (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which grammatical category indicates the time of an action?
questions.explanation: Tense refers to the changes in the form of verbs to show the time of an action (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which voice shows the subject receiving the action of the verb?
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject is the receiver of the action (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which part of speech describes a noun or pronoun?
questions.explanation: An adjective is a word that describes a noun or a pronoun (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type is placed before a noun to modify it?
questions.explanation: Attributive adjectives occur before a noun to pre-modify it (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type is placed after a linking verb?
questions.explanation: A predicative adjective is placed after the noun it modifies, often after a linking verb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which degree of comparison compares two items?
questions.explanation: The comparative degree is used to compare two items (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type describes the quality or kind of a noun?
questions.explanation: Descriptive adjectives are used to describe nouns or pronouns (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type points to specific nouns like this or that?
questions.explanation: Demonstrative adjectives indicate persons or things referred to (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type shows ownership like my or their?
questions.explanation: Possessive adjectives show possession (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type is used to ask questions like which or whose?
questions.explanation: Interrogative adjectives are used for asking questions (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type denotes number like one, two, or first?
questions.explanation: Numerical adjectives are used to denote the number of nouns (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which order correctly arranges multiple adjectives before a noun?
questions.explanation: The standard order of adjectives is opinion, size, age, shape, color, and noun (Quirk & Greenbaum).

questions.question: Which adjective type can be used in comparative or superlative forms?
questions.explanation: Gradable adjectives describe qualities that can be measured in degrees (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adjective type does not occur in comparative or superlative forms?
questions.explanation: Non-gradable adjectives describe qualities that are completely absent or present (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which part of speech modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb?
questions.explanation: An adverb modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adverb type answers the question when an action occurs?
questions.explanation: Adverbs of time answer the question when an action occurs (Muonagor).

questions.question: Which adverb type introduces a new sentence or links ideas?
questions.explanation: Conjuncts are adverbs that help to introduce new sentences or link ideas (Muonagor).
